newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK people's confidence in future falling - poll.
newsitem.headline: HK people's confidence in future falling - poll.

text.p: Fewer people in Hong Kong are optimistic about the territory's imminent return to Chinese rule than two months ago, according to the results of an opinion poll published on Tuesday.
The telephone poll for the daily South China Morning Post showed that about 57 percent of 586 people polled said they would be "happy" on June 30, the eve of Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule.
That marks a drop of nine percentage points from a similar survey in February. Those who said they were "saddened" by the sovereignty change rose to 17 percent from 11 percent.
The English-language newspaper said it was the first decline in good feelings about the handover since August last year.

Respondents, interviewed last week, were also cautious about political freedoms in the territory of 6.4 million people when it becomes part of China again after more than 150 years of British colonial rule, it said.
About 48 percent were confident about political liberties in the next 12 months, while 44 percent were not.
But respondents were upbeat about the territory's freewheeling capitalist economy and their personal finances.
The poll found almost 78 percent thought the economic future would be good. Only 14.4 percent thought the ouotlook was gloomy.

Two other polls in recent days have suggested the popularity of post-colonial leader Tung Chee-hwa has fallen since his office last week issued a plan to curb the right to demonstrate and ban foreign funding of Hong Kong political groups.
